A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching SAT reductions, circuit-size separation results, and inference guarantees. Their main text, equations, figure, table, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical results and counterexamples, including Appendices A–F. Figure 1 illustrates a circuit, and Table 1 reproduces mathematical properties from cited work; neither reports original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout its main text and appendices. Its added NeurIPS checklist also explicitly states that the paper contains no experiments.

M1.justification: The circuit classes, Sauerhoff-based construction, and edge-bound pruning procedure are retained. The pruning description moves from Appendix E.3 to Appendix A.3.2 without changing its steps.

E1.justification: Neither version uses training or evaluation datasets or benchmarks. Boolean formulas and distribution families serve as theoretical constructions, not evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods experimentally. Additional model families named in v2 Section 3.2 illustrate the hardness result's applicability rather than introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental protocols, training budgets, evaluation splits, or testing procedures. Changes to mathematical assumptions are assessed under T1.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness experiments, or empirical case studies. The inference guarantees moved from v1 Appendix B to v2 Section 5 remain theoretical analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests. The added checklist marks experimental statistical significance as not applicable.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries, performance values, or rankings are added or revised. Table 1 retains the same divergence functions and convexity constants; changes to formal arguments are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 adds Definition 3.3 and reformulates v1 Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4 as Theorem 3.4 and Corollary 3.5 with explicitly unnormalized inputs and normalized approximation targets. Counterexample 1 replaces the global-maximum argument in Appendix F with an auxiliary-variable construction addressing every evidence assignment. Theorem 4.1's proof also revises epsilon accounting. These are localized formal refinements; the principal reductions, separation bound, and inference theorems persist.

C1.justification: Both versions claim NP-hardness for models supporting tractable marginals, an exponential separation between decomposable and deterministic decomposable PCs, and a characterization of inference guarantees. The broader title emphasizes generality already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 Section 3.2 explicitly connects unnormalized inputs to factor graphs and energy-based models, identifies additional tractable model families covered by the hardness argument, and states its KL-divergence 1/8 consequence. Section 6 adds that approximation becomes trivial when TV tolerance approaches 1. The conditional-inference limitations largely retain v1 Appendix B's interpretation.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies implementation settings, hardware measurements, or code/data access resources. The pruning procedure remains documented in both; the added checklist does not announce a resource release or access change.

R1.justification: v2 adds contextual references to probabilistic generating circuits, determinantal point processes, sum-of-squares, Inception and positive unital circuits, unnormalized models, and approximate counting. It drops the compositional-atlas reference. The central positioning against earlier circuit-succinctness and approximate-compilation results remains intact.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are substantially rewritten. PC background from Appendix A becomes Section 2.1, inference guarantees from Appendix B become Section 5, and several appendix proofs enter the main text. Sections gain subdivisions, remaining appendices are consolidated, and acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist are added.

P2.justification: The two-column main text and references become a single-column NeurIPS layout, and the separate supplementary title page disappears. Figure 1 moves into Section 2.1 with text wrapping. Table 1 is resized and recaptioned in Appendix A.1 while retaining its mathematical entries.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the hardness result's input-normalization assumptions explicit and supplies a MAP counterexample that addresses every evidence assignment, improving precision. Integrating background, proofs, and inference guarantees also improves readability. These are useful but limited gains because the principal theoretical results and proof strategies remain largely unchanged.
